prompt: A scatterplot relates the number of years since a tree was planted, $x$, to its height in feet, $y$. The line of best fit is $y = 1.8x + 4$. What does $1.8$ represent in this model?

choices.label: The height of the tree when it was planted
The predicted increase in height, in feet, per year
The total height of the tree after one year
The number of years for the tree to reach $1.8$ feet

hint: The slope is a rate: output units per input unit.

hints.text: The slope is a rate: output units per input unit.
Here that is feet per year.
$1.8$ is the predicted growth in feet for each additional year.

learningObjective: Interpret the slope of a line of best fit in context.
explanation: The slope of any linear model is the change in $y$ for a one-unit change in $x$.
With $y$ in feet and $x$ in years, the slope is measured in feet per year: the tree grows about $1.8$ feet each year.
Choice A describes the intercept ($4$ feet at planting). Choice C would be $1.8 + 4 = 5.8$ feet.

alternativeExplanations.title: Say the units out loud
steps: Slope units are always "$y$-units per $x$-unit" — here, feet per year.
Once you have said "feet per year", only one answer choice can match.
This works on every interpretation question in this area, and it takes about three seconds.
